FINDING_ID: IM_F701  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose()` computes the false-positive self-check even when the same call has already applied a self-adjustment in self-check 1. Location: `self_diagnose()`, after the low-remediation-success branch. Evidence from the shown code: self-check 1 sets `self._last_self_adjust_round = current_round` when it applies a widening adjustment, but execution continues into self-check 2 in the same invocation because the damping gate is only evaluated once near the top of the function. Therefore one call can still stack a second adjustment (`_sensitivity_decay`) on top of the first. This is distinct from the previously-found “same-call emission” issue because here the second branch performs an actual second parameter mutation, not just an extra diagnosis.  
PROPOSED_FIX: After any successful self-adjustment in self-check 1, return immediately from `self_diagnose()` (or gate later checks on a local `adjustment_applied` flag). Also do the same after self-check 2 if the intended policy is one self-adjustment per round.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F702  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.self_diagnose()` can repeatedly emit the “all self-adjustments rejected by extended P-pass” diagnosis every round from unchanged evidence, with no damping or deduplication. Location: `self_diagnose()`, `if not applied:` branch inside self-check 1. Evidence: that branch appends a WARNING diagnosis but does not update `_last_self_adjust_round` and does not record a rejection marker in `_self_diagnosis_history`. On the next round, if `len(self._remediation_outcomes) >= 3` and `success_rate < 0.3` still hold, the same branch runs again and emits the same diagnosis indefinitely. This is not covered by the known chain-exhaustion repetition issue; it is a separate repeated-meta-diagnosis path.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Record rejected self-adjustment attempts in `_self_diagnosis_history` and set a per-trigger cooldown (or reuse `_last_self_adjust_round`) even for rejected adjustments, so unchanged evidence does not re-emit the same diagnosis every round.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F703  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `false_positive_rate`’s round window is off by one and includes 11 rounds when the docstring says “last 10 rounds.” Location: `false_positive_rate` property, `start_round = max(0, current_round - window)`. Evidence: if `current_round == 10` and `window == 10`, `start_round` becomes `0`, and the predicate `fp["round"] >= start_round` includes rounds 0..10 inclusive, i.e. 11 rounds. The proportional-tail denominator approximation then uses `fraction = window / total_rounds`, which is based on 10/11, so numerator and denominator are windowed by different effective spans.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use `start_round = max(0, current_round - window + 1)` and apply the same inclusive convention everywhere the self-metrics claim a fixed N-round window.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F704  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `chain_exhaustion_rate` mixes incompatible windows and can exceed the intended recent-event horizon. Location: `chain_exhaustion_rate` property. Evidence: it uses `recent_outcomes = self._remediation_outcomes[-10:]` but `recent_exhaustions = self._chain_exhaustion_history[-5:]`, then divides `len(recent_exhaustions)` by the sum. The numerator and denominator are sampled from different horizons by construction. Two exhaustions from long ago can remain in the last-5 slice while many recent outcomes dominate the last-10 slice, or vice versa; the metric is not a coherent “recent rate.” This is separate from the already-known “mixed event types in denominator” flaw: even if mixed types were acceptable, the windows are still inconsistent.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Window both histories by the same round range or same event-count horizon before computing the ratio, e.g. “last 10 rounds” using stored `round` fields.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F705  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` never checks whether `response.model_id` is in `_active_models` before classifying failures and emitting events, so excluded models can continue generating TIMEOUT/EMPTY/MALFORMED/FORMAT events even if UNDERPERFORM is later suppressed elsewhere. Location: `detect_failure()`, entire method entry path. Evidence from shown code: `_active_models` is only updated in `get_recovery()` on exclusion, but `detect_failure()` performs all priority checks and `_emit_event()` calls unconditionally. Known findings already cover UNDERPERFORM on excluded models; this broader issue affects all failure classes and the event stream.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an early guard at the top of `detect_failure()` such as `if response.model_id not in self._active_models: return None` before any event emission or perf-history updates.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F706  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler._failure_history` and `_perf_history` are initialized only for models passed in `models`, but `role_map` is accepted independently and is later used as authoritative in several methods. Location: `FailureHandler.__init__()`. Evidence: `self.models = {m.model_id: m for m in models}` and both histories are seeded from `models`; there is no validation that every key in `role_map` appears in `models`. If a caller passes a response for a role-mapped model absent from `models`, `detect_failure()` reaches `recent_perfs = self._perf_history[response.model_id][-h:]` and raises `KeyError`. This is adjacent to, but distinct from, the previously found constructor contract issue that discussed later `AttributeError` paths; this one is a direct failure in shown immune code.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate in `__init__()` that `set(role_map).issubset(self.models.keys())`, raising `ValueError` on mismatch, or initialize internal histories from the union of both sets if that contract is intended.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F707  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` deduplicates `_perf_history` by `(model_id, round_idx)` only, which can suppress legitimate multiple underperformance observations for the same model in the same round when the round contains multiple tasks/subtasks. Location: `detect_failure()`, `key = (response.model_id, response.round_idx)`. Evidence: the interface summary shows `Task` allocation and decomposed dispatch exist outside the immune boundary; the same model can plausibly return multiple task responses in one round. With current dedup, only the first response contributes to `_perf_history`, so the persistence-window signal depends on call order rather than all observations.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either make the contract explicit that `detect_failure()` is called once per model per round with an already-aggregated `ModelResponse`, or include a task/subtask identifier in the dedup key and aggregate per-round performance before applying the underperformance predicate.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: IM_F708  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.check_dispatch_health()` computes verification miscalibration from lifetime means per model, so one fixed bad period can poison the detector indefinitely after a remediation succeeds. Location: `check_dispatch_health()`, construction of `model_means` from each full `rates` list. Evidence: for each model it does `m = sum(rates) / len(rates)` using the entire history. There is no recent window aligned with the monitor’s remediation verification or natural-resolution logic. A model that was miscalibrated for early rounds and then repaired will still carry that stale lifetime average forward, delaying or preventing natural recovery detection. This is separate from the already-known lifetime-average concern in prior findings if that one was treated as unverified; in the shown code this behavior is directly observable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute model means over a bounded recent window, e.g. last `persistence_window` or last N rounds, and use the same window for both flagging and recovery.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F709  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.validate_k1()`’s inline explanation contradicts the actual code and the configured default escalation threshold. Location: comments inside `validate_k1()`. Evidence: the code comment says “Second failure: ABORT (repeated)” and then immediately explains the second call is not repeated yet and a third call is needed. The method then uses a third call to assert ABORT. This is not runtime logic corruption, but it is internally contradictory verification documentation inside immune-layer code and can mislead maintenance of the failure policy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the comment block with a single consistent explanation that with `n_fail=2`, the second distinct occurrence is repeated once one prior matching record is in history, and adjust the test scenario or comment to match the actual call pattern being validated.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F710  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The artifact is insufficient to verify whether `process_round()` resets `FailureHandler.reset_round_state()` at each round boundary, whether `detect_failure()` is called once per model or once per task fragment, and whether model-level diagnoses are registered before `record_round()` in the current integration path. These contracts materially affect immune correctness for reallocation depth, underperformance deduplication, and false-positive accounting. Location: omitted `process_round()` body and surrounding orchestration. Evidence: the interface summary explicitly notes `process_round()` immune integration is in scope, but the body is not shown. I cannot honestly close these risks from the excerpt alone.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Review the full `process_round()` implementation and its call graph for: (1) round-boundary call to `failure_handler.reset_round_state()`, (2) aggregation semantics of `ModelResponse` passed into `detect_failure()`, and (3) ordering of `register_diagnoses()`, `record_model_round()`, and `record_round()`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE
